stopRules: Do not execute while the persistent lifetime headroom is lower than the complete 1.10 USD per-job cap; reserving only the first call is forbidden.
Do not change the 50 USD hard stop or treat account balance as mission authorization without another explicit user-funded budget extension.
Do not execute without a paid-tier observation less than 15 minutes old.
Stop before the first model call if branch, clean-tree rule, minimum commit, bank hash, local router binary, model or provider configuration differs.
Stop before the first model call if the reference corpus cannot be sealed or has an active ingestion job; reject the pilot if the postflight seal differs.
Stop at the persistent lifetime, 1.10 USD per-job or twenty-four-provider-call or forty-eight-documentary-call guard; never purchase or reload credits automatically.
Do not run repetitions two or three after a failed or semantically unreviewed first pilot.

validatedObservations: The category-aware Planner again used seven exact cuisine queries and one complementary unscoped query.
The run completed eighteen successful provider calls and forty documentary operations without transport or budget failure.

Candidate Judge round nine refined a subordinate SEMMELKNÖDEL title to the complete exact line SEMMELKNÖDEL AUX LÉGUMES while another card from the same opaque source already used that complete identity.
The generic inventory parser rejected the two different candidate keys converging on one source identity before deterministic inventory merge, so the Writer was never called.
executionResult.cause: Two separately retrieved cards from the same source represented the same recipe. The Candidate Judge correctly refined the subordinate card title to the full exact identity, but ParseCandidateInventoryUpdates prohibited duplicate normalized identities inside the Judge batch before MergeCandidateInventory could consolidate them. This valid documentary deduplication case was misclassified as a Judge protocol failure.
